THE cycle to learn from. All 3 attempts returned done with honest green re-runnable gates and all 3 were wrong — every defect semantic, in a security predicate whose failure mode is silence. Review found: global WeakSet leaking a shared object's secret in plaintext; entropy rule destroying UUIDs/paths/shas; paused parts persisting the same tool args verbatim (a defect in MY task spec, not the worker's execution — the four-part-type list was wrong); Buffer/Map/Set bypassing the key rule; cycle back-edge embedding the original object; depth cap failing OPEN; and \b never firing inside access_token because _ is a word char. Supervisor repaired the last inline (lookarounds + a case-SENSITIVE camel pattern, since /i makes the lookbehind match T). Routing note: cursor is a good IC but cannot self-catch semantic security defects; the cross-family review is what earned this cycle, three times over.

THE design-signal cycle. Attempts 1-3 each closed the previous data-loss bug in enforceCeiling and introduced a different one in the SAME path: range regressed, then follow yielded the marker at its storage index (0,33T,30,31,32 - backwards), then the union merge over-extended and swallowed retained events. Three passes, three ways to lose retained events, one function => redesign, not a fourth patch. Deleted the stored marker; two monotonic counters + one shared readFromState. Reviewer: closed 'by deletion, not by patching'. Blocker class now unrepresentable because droppedTo derives from evicted REAL events. First real integration failure of the run: 4 slices cherry-picked clean, integrated gate showed 35 test fails + 1 TS error. Cause: packages/client/src/target.ts imported commander, declared in packages/cli — a phantom dependency Bun's hoisted node_modules hid in-repo and an isolated worktree exposed. Fixed as a layering violation, not a missing dep: argv parsing left the client entirely (connectionFlagsCommand/parseConnectionFlags/connectionFromArgs deleted), resolveHostedConnection/resolveHostedTarget now take a HostedConnectionInput object. Each surface parses its own args. 35 fails -> 1 -> 0. LESSON: a worktree is a stricter dependency check than the main tree; run the gate there before trusting it.

ALL TESTS PASSED AND THE FEATURE DID NOT WORK. Ran the binary before flipping: default kuralle send returned {status:waiting,view:{blocks:[]}} while the session store held a correct reply, and --stream hung 2min. Cause: buildDemoRuntime took 3 params, BuildRuntime passes 4, so it silently dropped the SessionEventLog — and send builds its TurnResult by REDUCING that log. The demo agent is the no---agent default, so this was the default path. Every test passed because each fixture runtime appends to the log ITSELF instead of letting createRuntime do it — the fixtures re-implemented the broken thing. Second defect visible only after the first: TurnResult.message joined ALL assistant blocks, so --resume re-emitted every earlier reply glued to the new one. Added Runtime.getEventLog() so wiring is assertable without a model. Both tests confirmed red with their fix reverted. This is the third time this session that green-by-construction fixtures hid a real defect.

kuralle memory returned empty on a live agent. NEARLY FILED A FALSE POSITIVE: DEFAULT_EXTRACTION_TRIGGER is {tokens:2000}, so one short turn is below threshold BY DESIGN. Underneath it was a real defect though — with trigger:'each-turn' extraction still wrote nothing. Extraction is background work (core's own late-extraction.test.ts asserts streamExtractionCount===0 then awaits runtime.settled()); send never called settled(). One turn per process means the process boundary IS the turn boundary, so the fact was lost with no error. Measured: WITHOUT settled 0 files written, WITH settled 1. Existing memory tests all seed extractedValueStore.save() directly and read it back, never crossing the runtime's write path. New test uses a deliberately slow store so the race is deterministic, not timing-dependent. Adding settled() broke 8 CLI tests whose fixtures cast Pick<Runtime,'run'|'abortSession'> as Runtime — an explicit lie to the type system; widened the Pick instead of guarding the call.

Rail shipped and verified (frame-level assertions + ran the binary; OpenTUI Zig FFI initialises, paints, exits clean). But its third validation item — hosted parity, REQ-10 — was VACUOUS: both sides of the comparison were MockSession built from the same helper with the same args, so it could not fail. Same failure shape as t15's parity test earlier this run. Replaced with a Bun.serve stub serving the versioned turn route as SSE, driving the real httpTransport. Proved it discriminates by reversing frame order. The real test then exposed a wire-format gap: LoggedEventSequencer stamps at:Date.now() on receipt, so server timestamps never cross the versioned send route — a 200ms tool span reduces to ms:0 over HTTP, in the rail AND the transcript's tool block. Test strips ms/startedAt with a comment; gap filed as its own task. PATTERN: when two sides of a parity assertion are built by the same helper, it is not a test.

Brief specified the splice approach explicitly (no re-serialisation — serializeOnce exists because a part may carry getters that must not run twice) and the worker followed it exactly, both normal and poison paths. Supervisor independently re-ran the revert-proof: all 3 tests red with the fix reverted. One review fix inline: the stability test re-implemented sha256/32 and asserted f(x)===f(x), a tautology; rewrote it to blank the id in the raw persisted line and recompute, which tests the derivation rather than the algorithm.
